title: Telemetry Canvas + Autoscale Controls for Dedicated GPU Pools
creator: Laura Kim
description: Design a consolidated telemetry canvas and control surface for Dedicated GPU pools focused on pool health, autoscaling presets, and burst/buffer settings. This ticket covers surface-level sketches, mid-fidelity prototypes, accessibility checks, and a final design handoff package for engineering. Goals: make pool status and actionable controls discoverable, provide safe defaults and explorable advanced options, and surface estimated cost impact for changes.
user_stories: As a platform engineer I want a single view showing GPU pool health (utilization, memory pressure, eviction rate) so I can quickly evaluate pool stability.
As an SRE I want autoscale presets with SLO-aligned recommendations so I can adopt safe scaling behavior without trial and error.
As a product owner I want a burst budget control that limits temporary capacity spikes to a predictable cost impact so we can enable occasional load surges without blowing budget.
As a console user I want to preview the estimated per-hour and per-day cost delta when changing autoscale or burst settings so I can make informed decisions.
As an operator I want logs and recent incidents linked from the pool view so I can investigate anomalies without switching tools.
acceptance_criteria: A mid-fidelity prototype exists for the pool telemetry canvas with the following panels: summary bar, health sparkline, node distribution, eviction/oom rate, active batch sizes, and top 3 alerts.

There is a control panel supporting: autoscale presets (SLO-focused, cost-focused, custom), a burst budget slider with explicit cost preview, and an emergency manual scale button with confirmation flow.
Cost preview uses the current pricing model (tokens/minute + GPU-hour) and shows a 1-hour/24-hour estimate; numbers are annotated with assumptions.
Design includes default safety constraints (max burst percentage, cooldown windows) and clearly visible warnings when a configuration risks SLA violations.
Design passes basic accessibility audit: color contrast, keyboard focus order for controls, and descriptive aria text for status widgets.
Design deliverables include Figma frames, an annotated handoff doc, accessibility notes, and a short interaction video (30s) showing autoscale change flow.
Dependencies and implementation notes are documented for engineering handoff.

decisions: Prefer a compact 'summary bar' at the top with: status chip (Healthy/Degraded/Critical), current vCPU/GPU utilization, and active alerts count.
Autoscale presets will be three quick choices: 'SLO-aligned' (recommended), 'Cost-optimized', and 'Custom'. Each preset explains trade-offs and estimated cost impact.
Bursting is controlled by a budget slider + explicit policy modal. Maximum burst default set to 20% of pool capacity with a 15-minute cooldown window.
Manual scale operates at pool-level only and requires a two-step confirmation on production pools; an opt-in bypass is offered to admins with RBAC.
notes_for_engineering: Provide a lightweight REST hook to fetch pricing assumptions for cost preview (endpoint + example payloads in PRD).
Expose current pool telemetry metrics: GPU_util_pct, mem_pressure_pct, eviction_rate, batch_size_histogram, node_count, ready_node_count.
Autoscale presets map to policy JSON; include sample policy schemas in handoff doc.
Confirm RBAC rules for manual scale and burst policy edits; default to admin-only for production pools.
